solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fun run is so long

blocks.note: good = enjoyable, as in 'good fun'
in cricket a bye is a run scored without the batter hitting the ball

explanation.surface: A charity fun run that drags on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: "So long" reads as a complaint about the race's length, but it is the farewell. Cricket, played across Britain and the Commonwealth, has several kinds of run; a bye is one.
explanation.definitionFit: "So long" is an informal farewell, the casual equivalent of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Collected gallons poured out

blocks.note: g is the abbreviation for gallons
the six letters of POURED, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pouring out gallons of liquid that had been collected.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures liquid, and "poured out" reads as one phrase; split it and "out" is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of gathered together: collected items are grouped in one place.

clue.text: Mind private investigator eating vegetable? On the contrary

indicators.note: what eats takes the other thing inside itself
says the opposite of what was just stated is true, so the eater and the eaten swap places

blocks.note: a common vegetable; it does the eating
PI = private investigator; this goes inside

explanation.surface: A detective munching a vegetable, and someone asking whether you mind.
explanation.walkthrough: "On the contrary" reads like a retort to the question mark, but it turns the eating round. "Mind" looks like a verb; it is the noun, as in "to my mind".
explanation.definitionFit: Mind as a noun can mean view, as in "to my mind" or "change your mind", which is an opinion.

clue.text: Made bishop regret going topless

indicators.note: topless means without a top, and in a down answer the top is the first letter

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation
GUILT, regret, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A newly appointed bishop wishing he had not stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: "Made bishop" reads as a promotion, but "Made" alone is the definition and "bishop" starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of constructed: a house that was made was built.

clue.text: Crucial German city territory infantry almost liberated at first

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so take the opening letter of the four words before it

blocks.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
first letters of territory, infantry, almost, liberated

explanation.surface: A wartime report of a vital German city, its territory nearly freed by the infantry.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime picture makes "liberated" and "almost" look like part of the story, but each only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something crucial cannot be done without, which is what essential means.

clue.text: Almost putting up with small, dried fruit

indicators.note: almost all of a word falls just short of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: RAISING, putting up, without its last letter
S = small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone nearly tolerating a small portion of dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Putting up with" looks like one phrase meaning tolerating; split it and "putting up" is lifting something, with "with" just joining.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: these are grapes that have been dried, one of the commonest dried fruits.

clue.text: Thieves pinching second of her gowns

indicators.note: pinching is stealing, taking something into your grasp, so one piece holds another
the letter in second position of the next word

blocks.note: the verb: he thieves, he robs
second letter of hEr

explanation.surface: Burglars stealing a woman's gowns.
explanation.walkthrough: "Thieves" looks like a plural noun but is the verb, and "pinching" plays along with the theft while really meaning holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: long loose ceremonial or dressing gowns are called robes.

clue.text: Shows distance I moved

indicators.note: the letters are moved out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A walker's app showing how far they travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: "Distance I moved" reads naturally as how far I went; "moved" is doing the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sign or gauge that shows something indicates it.

clue.text: Ape that is gathering moist earth, oddly

indicators.note: odd here means odd-numbered, so take letters 1, 3, 5 and so on

blocks.note: i.e. = that is
letters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 of MOISTEARTH

explanation.surface: A gorilla collecting damp soil.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ape" looks like the animal, but it is the verb, to copy. The odd letters run across both words, three from moist and two from earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ape as a verb means to copy someone's behaviour, as apes were thought to mimic people.

clue.text: Feel not quite right

blocks.note: a verb: to feel or believe something is so, as in "I feel he is lying"
an adjective: dubious, as a dodgy package is

explanation.surface: Someone saying they are feeling a bit off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, it sounds like feeling unwell; the two halves are a verb and an adjective with nothing linking them.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to feel something is so without proof; as an adjective, suspect means dubious or not quite right.

clue.text: Starts with nothing right before one drinks

blocks.note: O = zero, nothing
R = right, placed before what follows
I = one, the Roman numeral
measures of gin

explanation.surface: Someone who begins the day with no alcohol, right up until having a few.
explanation.walkthrough: "Starts" looks like a verb but is the plural noun, beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the starts of things, their beginnings or sources, are their origins.

clue.text: Change one’s mind about island’s birds

blocks.note: to budge is to shift position, including in an argument
I = island goes inside; the 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: Someone revising their opinion of an island's birds.
explanation.walkthrough: "Change one's mind about" reads as one phrase; "about" is really the container instruction. Budgies, short for budgerigars, are small pet parrots.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: budgerigars are small Australian parrots, among the most popular pet birds.

clue.text: Giant pins fixed things on the gallery walls

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or rearranged, as a fixed match is, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Oversized pins fixing exhibits in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fixed" looks like the pins doing their job of fastening; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: what hangs on gallery walls is mostly framed paintings.

clue.text: Pursue patient outside hospital

blocks.note: a doctor's case is a patient
H = hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Going after a patient who has walked out of hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: "Patient" looks like it could be an adjective, but it is the noun: a case on a doctor's list.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pursue someone is to chase after them.

clue.text: Ecstasy after desperate fellow caught ball

blocks.note: Desperate Dan, the strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy
c = caught in cricket scoring
E = the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A frantic man, high on ecstasy, catching a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball looks like something to catch; it is a formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a grand formal occasion for dancing, so a ball is a kind of dance.

clue.text: Plant I weed less vigorously

indicators.note: done with energy, so the letters are stirred up hard into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gardener admitting they weed less energetically than before.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plant" sits comfortably in a gardening scene, where it could be an instruction; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: edelweiss is a white alpine flower, national symbol of Switzerland and Austria.

clue.text: Restless naughty child and adult I found in teepee?

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so I goes inside the tent

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
A = adult, the old film certificate
a teepee is a kind of tent
goes inside TENT after the T

explanation.surface: A fidgety child and a grown-up camping in a wigwam.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a teepee is only one example of a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone restless cannot wait calmly, which is what being impatient means.

clue.text: Area on crest for bird

indicators.note: on top of, and in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: a part of town is an area
the crest of a hill is its ridge

explanation.surface: A bird-spotter's note about a feathered crest.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crest" suggests feathers on a bird's head; it is a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the partridge is a plump game bird of fields and moors.

clue.text: Tourist’s rant nearly boring bank employee

definitions.note: Tourist's = tourist is; the 's links the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: nearly all of a word, so its last letter is dropped
boring as drilling, so one piece bores into another

blocks.note: a teller serves customers at a bank counter
RAVE, to rant, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker ranting at a dull bank clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring" looks like a comment on the bank employee's personality; it means drilling into them.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tourist is one kind of traveller.

clue.text: Casual garments mistress finally lowered, producing urges

indicators.note: moved lower, and in a down answer lower means further along

blocks.note: T-shirts are casual tops
last letter of mistresS, which is also the second letter of the garments

explanation.surface: A mistress slipping off casual clothes, stirring desire.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that sits second in the garments drops down below the R. "Urges" looks like a verb; it is the plural noun, cravings.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is used figuratively for any strong craving, as in a thirst for knowledge, so thirsts are urges.

clue.text: Complaint from mail I’m sent, each denied opening

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so every word is refused its first letter

blocks.note: mAIL without its first letter
I'M without its first letter
sENT without its first letter

explanation.surface: A grumble about letters that were sent but never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: "Complaint" looks like a grievance about the post; it is an illness. "Denied opening" also looks like unopened mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint, in the medical sense, is a minor illness such as a chest complaint.

clue.text: Partly thinks of a reason to date

indicators.note: only in part, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: thinkS OF A Reason

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly coming up with an excuse for a date.
explanation.walkthrough: "To date" looks like arranging a romantic outing; it means up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: "to date" means up to the present moment.

clue.text: Mark’s exploit on river

definitions.note: Mark's = mark is; the 's links the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: on top of, and in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: an exploit is a daring deed
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A man called Mark performing some daring deed on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mark" poses as a man's name; it is a distinguishing mark. The Ure is a crossword favourite among rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguishing mark, the thing that sets something apart, is one of its characteristic points.

clue.text: Particular thoughtfulness

blocks.note: the noun, a detail or point, as in "in every particular"
regard or consideration shown to others

explanation.surface: A fussy kind of consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: "Particular" looks like an adjective, fussy; it is the noun, a point or detail.
explanation.definitionFit: "In every particular" and "in every respect" mean the same; respect is also regard for others' feelings.

clue.text: Relative from Northern Ireland returned with coppers

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: NI = Northern Ireland
the law = the police; coppers is British slang for police officers

explanation.surface: A relative coming back from Belfast escorted by police.
explanation.walkthrough: "Returned with coppers" suggests a police escort; "returned" only works on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: an in-law is a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Italians perhaps could make one a purse

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something new by rearranging them

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Italian craftsmen, famous for leather goods, who could make you a purse.
explanation.walkthrough: "Perhaps" marks Italians as one example rather than the whole class.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Italians are one nationality among Europeans.

clue.text: Some sly men enjoy upsetting opponent

indicators.note: only some of the words, so the answer is a part of them
upset means knocked over, so in a down answer the letters are turned upside down

blocks.note: slY MEN Enjoy, then read upwards

explanation.surface: Sneaky men who like to annoy their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: "Upsetting" reads as annoying the opponent; it is the instruction to turn the letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an opponent in a fight or a war is the enemy.

clue.text: Dads regularly seem old-fashioned

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: pa = dad
S and E, letters 1 and 3 of SEEM

explanation.surface: Fathers who routinely come across as out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: "Regularly" looks like it describes how often dads seem dated, but it works on seem.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing: passé, literally past, is used in English for something out of fashion.

clue.text: Check short needle is disinfected

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: STEM, to check a flow, without its last letter
to needle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: A nurse checking that a short needle has been sterilised.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes "needle" a syringe; it is the verb, to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something disinfected has been freed of germs, and sterile means germ-free.

clue.text: Daughter is placed last in race, creating argument

indicators.note: the last letter in the word that follows

blocks.note: d = daughter, as in family trees
used as it stands
placed = put down
last letter of racE

explanation.surface: A daughter finishing last in a race, sparking a row.
explanation.walkthrough: "Placed last" reads as a race result; "placed" is its own piece and "last" works on race.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dispute is a disagreement or argument.

clue.text: Please speak about broken fist

blocks.note: to speak is to say
the four letters of FIST, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone begging a person to talk about their injured hand.
explanation.walkthrough: "Please" opens the sentence like a polite request; it is the verb, to give pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to please someone is to meet their wishes, which is to satisfy them.

clue.text: Touch wire in electric heater?

blocks.note: the noun: a trace, as in "a touch of irony"
the coil that glows when the heater is on

explanation.surface: A warning not to touch the hot wire in a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: "Touch" reads as an instruction; it is a noun, a trace. The question mark shows the heater is one example of where this wire is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch of something is an element of it; the heating wire in a kettle or heater is also called the element.
